business_problem: Unlocking scale and flexibility New Aim built Dropshipzone on the Community Edition of MongoDB, which came with the eCommerce solution Magento (now Adobe Commerce).
solution_summary: Unlocking scale and flexibility New Aim built Dropshipzone on the Community Edition of MongoDB, which came with the eCommerce solution Magento (now Adobe Commerce). Migrating to MongoDB Atlas to manage data complexity and boost operational efficiencies New Aim migrated to MongoDB Atlas In August 2024. Building Dropshipzone on MonogDB Community Edition allowed the team to take advantage of MongoDB's document model, and quickly build an incredibly innovative platform. Over 200 suppliers are contributing to the New AIm marketplace today, and the number of SKUs it lists is over 100,000. The process was smooth, without any data losses or disruptions to New Aim’s operations. Since December 2024, MongoDB Atlas has been powering many of Dropshipzone’s applications and capabilities. “MongoDB Atlas’s document database model is helping our team manage the very complex data architecture that we have built over the years,” said Lau.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Retrieves semantically relevant context from New Aim's data for AI, search, and recommendation workflows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Provides relevance-based text retrieval across New Aim's documents and application data.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the customer, catalog, and interaction data that powers New Aim's personalized user experiences.

data_flow: Business documents, tickets, records, and other operational content stay in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search and MongoDB Atlas Search, where search indexes or vector embeddings are built and then queried in real time to supply grounded results to applications, assistants, or discovery features. Upstream and downstream integrations include APIs.
